package_info.why_malicious: These packages exploit dependency confusion to target internal developer environments. Upon installation, they attempt to download and execute code from external servers or exfiltrate system information. While these are PoC/bug bounty exercises, the behaviors are consistent with supply chain attack techniques and pose a risk if used in production environments.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (as soon as the package is required/installed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Attempts to contact an external server upon installation to check if the package is being executed, likely for tracking successful dependency confusion attacks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Initiates an unsolicited outbound HTTP request to an external domain during installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not contact arbitrary external servers during install/import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or update checks in legitimate packages, but these are usually opt-in and well-documented.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (as soon as the package is required/installed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Collects system information (CPU, home directory, hostname, username, DNS servers, package name/version) and exfiltrates it via HTTPS POST to an external server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Gathers sensitive host information and sends it to an external domain without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not exfiltrate system or user data on install/import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Crash reporting or telemetry, but only with user opt-in and privacy policy.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST to untrusted domain

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed due to dependency confusion (internal name collision).
Upon installation/import, package executes code to contact external server (zettle-bo) or exfiltrate system info (airbnb).
attack_chain.leads_to: External server receives notification or system data

attack_chain.action: For zettle-bo: External server logs successful installation (potential for further payload delivery). For airbnb: Attacker receives exfiltrated system information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attackers gain knowledge of internal environment or successful dependency confusion

behavioral_signatures: Network requests to hardcoded external domains during install/import
Collection and exfiltration of system/user information at install/import time
Unsolicited HTTP/HTTPS POSTs to non-standard domains
file_indicators: Presence of app.js or index.js with outbound network code in package root
References to external domains in code (e.g., .oast.pro, .lupin.com)
Suspicious package names mimicking internal dependencies
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests during npm install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that initiate outbound network connections during installation or import, especially to domains not associated with the package's legitimate vendor. Flag packages that collect and transmit system or user information without explicit user consent. Use static analysis to detect hardcoded external domains and dynamic analysis to observe network activity during package installation.
